title: responder-latency-profiler-and-differential-runbook-optimizer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add a responder latency profiler and a differential runbook optimizer that suggests step reordering and trimming based on historical responder timings and success rates. Includes new CLI subcommands and a minimal web UI; non-breaking telemetry schema bump handled by compatibility layer.
description: This PR introduces two related operator-facing features: a lightweight responder latency profiler that aggregates responder execution timing and cold-start costs across on-call shifts, and a differential runbook optimizer that proposes runbook edits (reorder, collapse, or annotate steps) based on observed latencies, flakiness, and paid-on-call cost heuristics. Motivation: customers repeatedly ask for tooling to reduce mean mitigation time and to pinpoint responders or steps that add disproportionate latency. The profiler collects anonymized, sample-rate-controlled timing across live playbook runs and exposes per-step and per-responder histograms. The optimizer consumes those histograms plus recent incident outcomes to generate ranked suggestions (e.g., move step B before step C, collapse steps D/E into a single scripted step, mark step F as optional under high-latency conditions). Key behaviors: sampling defaults to 5% for hosted, 20% for private deployments (configurable); suggestions are conservative and include an estimated impact score and a safety flag if a step has single-point-of-failure semantics. The change is designed to be opt-in; operators must run `sloctl runbook analyze --enable-optimizer` or toggle in the UI to accept suggestions. Implementation notes: new profiler agent (Go) runs as a small sidecar that emits compressed timing events to the existing telemetry pipeline; we've added a compatibility shim in the telemetry consumer to accept the new event type without breaking older consumers. The optimizer logic lives in the slo-toolkit service as a separate worker that runs differential comparisons between time windows and scores changes with a multi-factor heuristic (latency delta, responder variance, historical rollback rate). UI/CLI additions: `sloctl responder profile` (aggregates/store), `sloctl runbook preview --diff` (shows optimizer proposals), and a simple React panel under Oncall -> Runbooks that lists suggestions and provides one-click apply/draft actions (chains through the existing runbook API). Testing and validation: unit coverage for optimizer heuristic and careful e2e smoke tests using the incident-sim harness; added property tests to ensure optimizer never suggests removing steps with >99.9% success dependency tags. Performance: the profiler sidecar adds ~1% CPU and <1ms p99 overhead on the control path in our lab runs; optimizer job processed 10k incidents in ~7m on a standard worker (avg 45ms per incident in the scoring phase). Operational concerns and mitigations: sampling prevents high-volume customers from excessive telemetry; suggestions are never auto-applied unless explicitly enabled by policy; we added an audit trail and rollback link for applied suggestions. Migration: telemetry schema bump is guarded by a feature flag and consumer shim; rollout plan is staged by tenant with a gradual ramp and guardrails. Related work items: ENG-4189 (responder profiling), ENG-4221 (runbook optimizer prototype), SUP-1182 (customer request from enterprise support). Notes on security and privacy: payloads are hashed and only timing and low-cardinality metadata are retained; the feature is disabled by default for private/on-prem installs until customers opt in. Cherry-picks and hotfixes: small follow-up hotfix (see commits) fixed a race in the sidecar shutdown logic discovered in integration tests. Merge strategy: squash and merge after sign-off. See changed files list and review comments for specifics.

ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (flaky e2e initially failed then reran and passed)
notes_for_release: Opt-in feature behind flags. Runbook suggestions require operator approval before applying. Telemetry sampling defaults are conservative. Documented in docs/runbook-optimizer.md.
post_merge_tasks: monitor: onboarding metric for suggestions accepted vs reverted
observe: telemetry ingestion queue size for profiler events
follow-up: add tenant-level sampling UI control (ENG-4302)
testing_summary: Unit tests cover scoring heuristics; integration smoke validated safe suggestion generation; e2e acceptance simulated 500 distinct incidents to validate no unsafe removals. QA verified fix for sidecar shutdown race and replayed event streams to ensure no consumer breakage.
user_impact: Low by default (opt-in). Customers enabling profiler will see additional runbook suggestion cards in the console; suggestions include estimated time-saved and confidence score.
how_to_rollout: Stage rollout: feature-flag off for all tenants -> enable for internal and 2 pilot tenants -> monitor metrics for 2 weeks -> enable wider rollout. CLI users can opt in per-tenant using `sloctl feature enable runbook-optimizer`.
security_considerations: Sensitive payload fields are hashed and truncated before emission. Sampling and tenant opt-in protect data volume. Private/on-prem installs default to disabled until explicit opt-in.
